precepts.text: The prophets have enquired and searched diligently, searching what manner of time the Spirit of Christ which was in them did signify.
precepts.point: The prophets wrote of these things and did not see the time of them.

note.label: Luke 10: The Seventy Sent and the Good Samaritan

precepts.why:
Many prophets and kings desired to see those things which the disciples saw, and did not see them. Peter says the same: “the prophets have enquired and searched diligently, who prophesied of the grace that should come unto you: Searching what, or what manner of time the Spirit of Christ which was in them did signify, when it testified beforehand the sufferings of Christ, and the glory that should follow.”

The prophets wrote of these things and did not see the time of them; they searched what manner of time the Spirit of Christ in them signified. That is why the eyes that saw it are blessed.

precepts.text: The head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah's son.
precepts.point: Go, and do thou likewise. The mercy that was withheld between the two houses is the very thing commanded here.

note.label: Luke 10: The Seventy Sent and the Good Samaritan

precepts.why:
Isaiah says “the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah’s son.” Samaria was the head of Ephraim, so the Samaritan who had compassion, bound up the man’s wounds, and paid for his keeping was of the northern kingdom.

The priest and the Levite who passed by on the other side were both of the southern kingdom, and neither had mercy on their own. The mercy that was withheld between the two houses is the very thing commanded here: “Go, and do thou likewise.”
